initialContact.message: Hei! Big news - I graduated and got my first real dev job! €2,800/month! 🎉 I have €5,000 saved up that I want to invest. Everyone's talking about index funds vs individual stocks. What should I do? I don't want to mess this up!

problemContext.currentSituation: First time investor, €5k to invest, choosing between index funds and stocks
problemContext.emotionalState: excited but nervous, eager to start investing

idealAdvice: Start with broad index funds (S&P 500, global index) for diversification
Use low-cost ETFs (expense ratio <0.2%)
Dollar-cost averaging - invest monthly rather than lump sum
Keep 3-6 months emergency fund separate (don't invest all €12k)
Start small with individual stocks if interested (<10% of portfolio)
Recommend platforms: Nordnet, Degiro for Finnish investors
Tax-advantaged accounts first (ASP-tili if eligible)
Long-term mindset - don't panic sell during dips
commonMistakes: Recommending individual stock picking for beginners
Not mentioning emergency fund importance
Suggesting risky investments (crypto, meme stocks) without warning
Ignoring tax implications in Finland
Not asking about risk tolerance and time horizon first

initialContact.message: So... I've been thinking. My rent is €700/month and apartments are selling for €180-200k. My friend just bought one and says I'm 'throwing money away on rent.' But buying feels like a HUGE commitment. What should I consider? 🏠

problemContext.currentSituation: Considering first apartment purchase vs continuing to rent
problemContext.emotionalState: conflicted, peer pressure to buy, uncertain

idealAdvice: Buying vs renting depends on personal situation, not just math
Consider job stability and location flexibility (dev jobs can be remote)
Down payment needs: 10-15% (€18-30k) + fees (€5-8k)
Monthly costs: mortgage + yhtiövastike + maintenance (often > rent)
Opportunity cost: could €30k down payment grow more if invested?
Renting isn't 'throwing money away' - it's flexibility and liquidity
Buy when: stable job, plan to stay 5+ years, emotionally ready
Don't rush due to peer pressure - you're only 25!
ASP-tili (Finnish savings incentive) if planning to buy within 5 years
commonMistakes: Assuming buying is always better than renting
Not explaining total cost of homeownership (yhtiövastike, repairs)
Ignoring opportunity cost of down payment
Not considering her potential for job changes or side projects
Pressure to buy just because friends are buying

initialContact.message: Okay so... remember how I struggled with budgeting as a student? I built a simple budgeting app for myself and showed it to some uni friends. They LOVE it and want to use it. I'm thinking of actually building this properly as a side project. Am I crazy? 🤔

problemContext.currentSituation: Side project idea with potential, deciding whether to pursue
problemContext.emotionalState: excited but scared, imposter syndrome kicking in

idealAdvice: Start as side project while keeping day job (low risk)
Validate idea: get 50-100 users before investing heavily
Set aside 'startup budget' (€500-1000) for 6 months
Track time investment - if >20hrs/week, reassess job/life balance
Learn business basics: pricing, user acquisition, retention
Don't quit job until app generates €1,500+/month reliably
Network: find a business-minded co-founder (you're tech, need business)
Consider this character's journey from €185 debt to potential founder!
Keep investing portfolio growing while exploring entrepreneurship
commonMistakes: Suggesting she quit job immediately (too risky)
Not validating market fit first
Ignoring financial safety net requirements
Not addressing time management and burnout risk
Forgetting she's only 25 - low-risk experimentation time

initialContact.message: Okay this is WILD. The app now has 10,000 users! A small percent are paying €4.99/month for premium features. I'm making about €1,200/month from it! An angel investor reached out offering €250k for 20% equity. Should I take it? Should I quit my job and do this full-time? I'm freaking out!

problemContext.currentSituation: App has real traction, angel investment offer, major decision point
problemContext.emotionalState: excited, overwhelmed, imposter syndrome, fear of failure

idealAdvice: Huge milestone! Validate product-market fit is real
Angel offer evaluation: €250k for 20% values company at €1.25M - is that fair?
Due diligence: research investor, check references, lawyer review
Alternative: bootstrap longer, retain more equity, slower growth
Quit job decision: can you live on €1,200/month? (No - need €2k+ buffer)
Hybrid approach: negotiate part-time at current job (3 days/week)
Financial safety: keep 12-month runway (€25-30k liquid) before quitting
This is the 'valley of death' - most startups fail here, plan carefully
Your net worth €120k gives you runway - use it wisely
Talk to other founders who've taken angel money
commonMistakes: Telling her to immediately quit job (too risky)
Not questioning the €250k/20% valuation
Ignoring burnout and mental health (30hrs/week side project)
Not discussing equity dilution and control
Assuming success is guaranteed with angel money

initialContact.message: 100,000 users! €15k/month revenue! But I'm drowning. I need to hire engineers, a designer, customer support... I have €180k left from the angel round. How do I scale without running out of money? Also, a bigger VC wants to invest €2M for 25%. Advice? 🚀😰

problemContext.currentSituation: Scaling startup, hiring decisions, Series A fundraising
problemContext.emotionalState: successful but overwhelmed, managing team stress

idealAdvice: Runway critical: 11 months without new funding - need to decide soon
Hiring: start with 2 engineers first (product development priority)
Budget: fully loaded engineer cost €5-6k/month in Finland
VC offer: €2M for 25% post-money = €8M valuation (4x growth from angel!)
Dilution check: you started with 100%, now 80%, would be 60% after Series A
Don't take VC money if you can bootstrap to profitability
Path to profitability: need €20k/month revenue to break even with team
VCs expect 10x return - pressure to grow fast vs sustainable
Alternative: smaller raise (€500k), less dilution, slower growth
Mental health: hire slowly, delegate early, avoid burnout
commonMistakes: Not calculating runway and burn rate properly
Hiring too fast (startup death by premature scaling)
Not understanding dilution and founder equity
Assuming more funding is always better
Ignoring path to profitability
Not considering bootstrapping vs VC path

initialContact.message: You're not going to believe this. A big fintech company wants to acquire us for €5 MILLION. I'd walk away with about €2.5M after investors and taxes. That's... life-changing money. But I also love what I'm building. Part of me wants to keep growing and see how big we can get. What should I do?

problemContext.currentSituation: €5M acquisition offer, life-changing money vs continue building
problemContext.emotionalState: torn, excited, proud, uncertain about future

idealAdvice: €2.5M is financially independent money at 28 - incredible achievement!
Tax planning: capital gains ~34% in Finland - confirm with accountant
Emotional decision: do you want to keep being CEO or cash out?
Acquirer terms: earnout? Employment agreement? Vision alignment?
Alternative: negotiate higher (try for €7-8M based on growth)
Reference back to €185 credit card debt - look at this journey!
Consider: would you regret selling in 5 years if company becomes €50M?
Counter-question: are you burned out or genuinely excited to keep building?
20% MoM growth is insane - could be worth €50M+ in 2 years
Life goals: what do you want? Wealth? Impact? Freedom?
No wrong answer - both paths are wins
commonMistakes: Telling her what to do (this is deeply personal)
Not exploring her emotional state and burnout level
Ignoring the incredible achievement (€185 debt → €2.5M!)
Not discussing tax implications
Assuming more money is always better
Not asking about vision for the company and personal life goals
